request.spec: Change the customerCode format to '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the first three of the lastName, and NNNN a per-city 4-digit sequence (one more than the owners already in that city). Every value derived from the customerCode, such as the membership number, must be rebuilt on the new format. This changes the current customerCode and everything built from it.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Change the customerCode format to '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the first three of the lastName, and NNNN a per-city 4-digit sequence (one more than the owners already in that city). Every value derived from the customerCode, such as the membership number, must be rebuilt on the new format. This changes the current customerCode and everything built from it.

agent.result_text:
Done. The full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 test run, 0 failures).

## What changed

**`AssignCustomerCode.java`** — rewrote the format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (global sequence) to **`<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`**:
- `CITY3` — upper-cased first three letters of the owner's city
- `LAST3` — upper-cased first three letters of the last name (unchanged logic, now factored into a shared `prefix` helper)
- `NNNN` — a **per-city** 4-digit zero-padded sequence, computed as one more than the owners already in that city (counted via `OwnerRepository.findAll()`, matched case-insensitively), replacing the old global `findAll().size() + 1`

**`AssignMembershipNumber.java`** — no code change needed: it already builds the membership number as `<customerCode>-M<YY>` off `owner.getCustomerCode()`, so it automatically picks up the new format. I only refreshed the stale example in its Javadoc (`SMI-0007-M26` → `SYD-SMI-0007-M26`).

The new acceptance test `coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix` (asserting `customerCode` matches `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}`) passes, as does the rest of the suite.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The structure is clean and idiomatic for this codebase:

- **Right unit / cohesion.** `AssignCustomerCode` still does exactly one thing — compose the customer code — and the two new private helpers (`prefix`, `countInCity`) are tightly scoped to that job. The class isn't drifting into a catch-all.
- **Duplication removed, not added.** Extracting `prefix(...)` collapses what would otherwise be two copies of the "upper-cased first three chars" logic (city and lastName) into one helper. That's the additive, DRY move a maintainer would expect.
- **Consistent with the existing pattern.** `countInCity` iterates `ownerRepository.findAll()`, which mirrors the pre-existing `findAll().size()` approach rather than inventing a new repository query method — it stays in step with how this code already talks to the repository.
- **Derived value handled at the right altitude.** `AssignMembershipNumber` builds its value from the already-assigned `customerCode` string, so it correctly needs no logic change — only the javadoc example was refreshed to the new format. Rebuilding on the new format happens for free because the derivation is a pure function of `customerCode`, and the ordering note (`Runs after AssignCustomerCode`) still documents that dependency.
- **Naming** follows the project's `Assign<E>` / verb-plus-entity convention, and the javadoc on both classes was kept in sync with the new format.

No structural changes needed.
